Definition: properly, session; but used also concretely, an abode or locality
BiblicalUsage: A seat is a place to sit, and a dwelling is a place to live, and this word is both. Solomon's throne had stays on either side on the place of the seat, with lions standing beside it, and Amos warns men who cause the seat of violence to come near. Obadiah speaks to Edom, dwelling in the clefts of the rock, high and sure no one can bring him down.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe where you sit says where you trust. Solomon's seat was the throne of a king, Edom's seat was a rock he trusted more than God, and I hold that only one seat is safe.
